recentItems.title: "There Are No Safe Places Left Here": Head of Doctors Without Borders on Russian Terror
recentItems.description:
Healthcare under fire: how are lives being saved near the front line? Henry Keen speaks with Robin Meldrum, representative of Doctors Without Borders (MSF) in Ukraine, about the dangers facing medical workers and patients. The conversation covers attacks on hospitals and medical transport, the impact of FPV drones on the nature of injuries and evacuations, staff shortages, and the exhaustion of Ukrainian doctors. How do mobile clinics, emergency response teams, and evacuation trains operate? Around 500 MSF staff members are helping Ukraine by supporting hospitals, providing medical transportation, and assisting with rehabilitation. A look into daily work where providing medical care itself becomes dangerous.

recentItems.title: Lied to Putin — got a drone: General Grunas was eliminated after a fake ‘victory’
recentItems.description:
Operation "Vivaldi" near Lyman, strikes on Russian airfields and oil refineries, and Russia's fuel troubles. We analyze how Ukrainian forces are dismantling enemy logistics and disrupting plans to encircle the "fortress cities" of the Donetsk region. In this episode: reports on the death of a Russian general, damage to aviation, ammunition depots, and drone control posts. Why is Trump urging a halt to refinery strikes, and what do the US sanctions entail? We also discuss the limited capabilities of the Black Sea Fleet, joint drone production with the EU, and the development of the FREYJA missile defense system. How are pressures on the front line, in the rear, and across the economy impacting Russia's ability to sustain the war?

recentItems.title: Ukraine counters jet Shaheds with new drone technology! End of Russian air superiority?
recentItems.description:
Russia attacked Ukraine with two Zircon missiles, strike drones, and "Banderol" projectiles. On the night of September 19, the main targets of the attack were the Odesa and Kyiv regions. In total, the enemy launched 174 UAVs and drone-type missiles, with Ukrainian air defense neutralizing 141 targets. On the front lines, the occupiers attempted to break through Ukrainian defenses 213 times over the past day. Meanwhile, the Defense Forces struck Russian drone command posts, a training ground, and ammunition depots in the Donbas and Zaporizhzhia regions. Details of the night attack, air defense results, and strikes on enemy military facilities are in the news roundup.

recentItems.description:
Ukrainian ballistics, counterattacks near Lyman, and new protection against Russian missiles. In this issue: statements on FP-7 and FP-9 testing and potential strikes on military targets deep inside Russia. We analyze the actions of the Defense Forces in the Donetsk region, the strategic importance of Lyman, and the defense of fortress cities. Also featured: new appointments for Andriy Biletsky and Denys Prokopenko, as well as the prospects of the FREYJA ABM system. A separate segment focuses on the humanitarian catastrophe in occupied Oleshky: food and medicine shortages, attacks on humanitarian supplies, and barriers to evacuation.

recentItems.title: OIL, OLIGARCHS, SHADOW FLEET US Goes After Russia's War Chest - KREMLIN IN SHOCK!
recentItems.description:
New US sanctions against Russia and the strengthening of Ukrainian air defense. Zelenskyy calls for increased pressure on the Kremlin, while Washington has approved a potential $2.68 billion sale of equipment to Ukraine. Denmark accelerates aid, and Poland joins the anti-ballistic coalition. Russia attacked the Odesa, Kyiv, and Donetsk regions: homes and energy infrastructure were damaged. Why is there a shortage of Patriot missiles, and when will production increase? We discuss drones over the Luxembourg airport, the threat of Russian hybrid attacks in Europe, and the delivery of the first F-35 to Germany. How are allies strengthening the defense of Ukraine and Europe? Watch the full coverage of events in Ukraine and around the world in this episode.
